title: Witness transfinite_defined proves the function defined by transfinite recursion is unique
intent: Prove the unique existence (`exists!`) of the function defined by transfinite recursion on a well-ordering by supplying the named witness `transfinite_defined r T` for the existence half and the lemma `transfinite_unique` for the uniqueness half.

parent.name: transfinite_definition
parent.statement:
Theorem transfinite_definition r T:
  worder r -> exists! f, (transfinite_def r T f).

children.name: transfinite_defined_pr
children.statement:
Lemma transfinite_defined_pr r T: worder r ->
  transfinite_def r T  (transfinite_defined r T).
children.note: The existence half: the witness transfinite_defined r T satisfies transfinite_def. Its proof unfolds /transfinite_defined, applies transfinite_def_prop1 to transfinite_pr1 (the graph-level property of transfiniteg_defined), then closes the pointwise goal by fgraph_to_fun_restr. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the witness transfinite_defined r T satisfies transfinite_def r T

children.name: transfinite_unique
children.statement:
Lemma transfinite_unique r T : worder r -> 
  uniqueness (transfinite_def r T).
children.note: The uniqueness half. Its proof sends the two functions to their graphs via transfinite_def_prop2, obtains graph uniqueness from transfiniteg_unique, and lifts it back to function equality via function_exten1. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: two functions satisfying transfinite_def r T are equal

applicability.goal_shape: A unique-existence goal `exists! f, P f` whose two halves are already proved as named lemmas: a witness `w` with `P w` for the existence half, and a uniqueness lemma `forall f g, P f -> P g -> f = g` for the uniqueness half.
applicability.use_when: the witness is a named definition (here `transfinite_defined r T`, built by `choose` from a graph-level existence theorem) whose property is already a lemma; `unique_existence` is the view that turns `exists!` into `existence /\ uniqueness`, so the proof is a two-line `split` with one lemma citation per half.
applicability.avoid_when: the witness must be synthesised inline and has no property lemma yet (state the property as its own lemma first, as here); the uniqueness argument is not a uniform 'send to the graph' step and differs per pair; the two halves share a large common core (prove that core first rather than splitting at once).

consequences: The move creates two obligations, one per half of `exists!`: existence (discharged by supplying the witness `transfinite_defined r T` with `transfinite_defined_pr`) and uniqueness (discharged by `transfinite_unique`). Existence is itself deferred one level: the witness is defined by `choose` from `transfinite_exists1`, so the real content of existence lives below the glue. Naming the witness keeps its property a reusable lemma, which the file reuses in `transfinite_definition_stable`; an inline `exists` term would force that property proof to be repeated.
